analysis.investment_thesis: P/E of 7.84 implies an earnings yield near ~12.7%, which looks attractive on the surface, but the reported ROE of 0.26% means return on capital is nowhere near Magic Formula standards. Cheap alone is not enough — I need cheap AND good, and this is only (maybe) cheap.
key_strengths: Earnings yield ~12.7% (1/7.84) is above my 12% threshold on a P/E basis
High promoter holding at 73.78% signals skin in the game
Small base (69 Cr mcap) leaves room for operational scaling if execution improves
key_risks: ROE of 0.26% is catastrophic — fails the 'good business' leg of the Magic Formula
Commodity plastic pipes industry — low pricing power, thin margins, capital-intensive
2017-incorporated micro-cap with limited track record; data reliability and one-time items are a concern
red_flags: ROE of 0.26% vs. P/E of 7.84 is internally inconsistent — suggests depressed TTM earnings or data quality issue
No evidence of sustained high ROIC over 3+ years
Negligible DII participation (0.07%) — institutions aren't validating this
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on two dimensions: earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital (EBIT/invested capital). Using P/E 7.84 as a proxy, earnings yield sits around 12.7% — borderline attractive. But the second leg collapses: ROE of 0.26% is effectively zero, and for a manufacturer of commodity plastic pipes, ROIC is unlikely to be meaningfully better than ROE. A business earning nothing on its capital base destroys shareholder value over time regardless of how cheap the stock appears.

I systematically avoid buying "cheap" that isn't also "good." This one fails that test clearly. There may be a data reconciliation issue (the ROE/P/E combination is mathematically inconsistent for a profitable company), which only reinforces my discipline: when I cannot compute the two formula inputs with confidence, I pass. A plastic pipes micro-cap with no institutional validation and no evidence of high returns on capital is precisely the kind of name the Magic Formula is designed to filter out.
